# Was the Ochsner Health data breach a cyberattack?

**Confirmed.** Yes, by Ochsner's own account: an unauthorized party accessed two employee accounts on Sept 18 to 21 and downloaded files from one. How, by whom and how many people are affected are not established.

Incident: Ochsner Health data breach, Nov 19, 2026. Also reported as Ochsner data incident, Ochsner Microsoft 365 breach and Ochsner Vortex claim. First published Nov 21, 2026; last updated Nov 21, 2026, 9:40 AM ET.

> **Not verified: initial investigation only.** Nothing on this page is absolutely confirmed. It is an early look based only on publicly available sources, and it should not be treated as verified fact. Even items labeled "Confirmed" only mean a public source reports them. Made for entertainment using AI. Not endorsed by Ochsner Health, Orlando Health, any news outlet, government agency, company, or anyone else named.

This is the current answer, not a final verdict.

## The latest

Nov 21, 2026, 9:40 AM ET: **Researchers describe a healthcare extortion cluster called Vortex; it is not tied to Ochsner, and the method is still unknown.** Ochsner's notice is unchanged. Added Palo Alto Networks Unit 42's Nov 20 research on a cluster it calls Vortex (new c012, Reported, related only): it says the cluster targets healthcare through fake IT-support calls and fake sign-in pages to copy Microsoft 365 files. The report does not name Ochsner, so attribution (c006) and the method (c007) stay Not established. Added NOLA.com (same article as The Advocate) and IPCRIME. New question q008. No count of affected people, no Ochsner tie to Vortex, no Orlando Health statement and no report of care disruption. No label changes. Privacy check done.

## At a glance

- Status: monitoring
- Size: Regional. Ochsner is the largest health system in Louisiana, and says letters will go to people whose information is involved. It has not said how many people, so size rests on the organization's reach, not a count.
- Who is affected: People whose information was in the files downloaded from one of two Ochsner employee accounts. Ochsner says it is still working out who, and will send letters. It says patient care and its record systems were not disrupted.

| Value | What | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| 2 | Employee accounts accessed | Files downloaded from one, per Ochsner |
| Sept 18 to 21 | Access window | Ochsner learned of it on Oct 1 |
| About 25,000 | Files Vortex claims | A group's claim, not verified |

### Known so far

- Ochsner says an unauthorized party accessed two employee accounts in its Microsoft environment on Sept 18 to 21 and downloaded files from one.
- Ochsner learned of it on Oct 1, determined on Nov 18 that specific information was accessed, and began notifying people on Nov 19.
- The files may include names, demographic information, Social Security numbers and health information.
- Ochsner is offering one year of free credit monitoring to people whose Social Security numbers were involved.

### Not known yet

- How the two accounts were accessed, and who did it.
- Whether the group Vortex, which claims about 25,000 files, is behind it.
- How many people are affected.
- Whether a ransom was demanded or any data has been published.

## Related, but separate

| Claim | Label | What we know | Why it supports, and more detail | Sources |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Vortex also listed Orlando Health on Nov 19; we found no statement from Orlando Health | Unverified | PlayCISO reports Vortex named Orlando Health the same day as Ochsner and claims Microsoft 365 files and directory data. It found no statement from Orlando Health as of Nov 20. | One Tier 3 analysis relays a claim; no health-system statement or independent confirmation. This is a related note only. It rests on one analyst post that relays a leak-site listing, and it says nothing about an Ochsner link. | [PlayCISO: Ochsner, Orlando Health Named by Vortex: What We Know (independent analysis; did not visit the leak site)](https://playciso.com/blog/ochsner-orlando-health-vortex-leak-site-claim) |
| Palo Alto Networks Unit 42 says a new extortion cluster it calls Vortex targets healthcare organizations by posing as IT support on the phone to get into Microsoft 365 accounts; its report does not name Ochsner | Reported | Unit 42 says the cluster, first seen in September 2026, mainly targets healthcare. Callers pose as IT support, send staff to fake sign-in pages, add their own login device, then copy Microsoft 365 mail, OneDrive and SharePoint files. | Unit 42 (Tier 3 vendor research) reports it from its own incident-response work; IPCRIME summarizes it and notes the limits. This describes the cluster's general methods across many targets. Unit 42 does not name Ochsner or Orlando Health, and nothing in the report shows the group that listed Ochsner is the cluster Unit 42 tracks, or that Ochsner's accounts were accessed this way. | [Palo Alto Networks Unit 42: Dialing for Data: Inside the Com's High-Profile Heists (does not name Ochsner)](https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/com-affiliate-vishing-attacks/), [IPCRIME: Ochsner Health Discloses Downloaded Files After Two Employee Accounts Were Compromised](https://www.ipcrime.com/2026/11/20/ochsner-health-employee-account-breach-downloaded-files-2026/) |

## What we checked and did not find

We looked for these and did not find them as of our latest check on Nov 21.

- A description of how the two accounts were accessed, or of the attacker, from Ochsner or any regulator.
- A count of the people affected, from Ochsner, a state attorney general or a federal breach filing. We found no Louisiana or federal filing in the coverage we read.
- Any statement from Ochsner tying the incident to Vortex, or confirming a ransom demand or publication of data.
- Any outlet, patient or staff report of a disruption to care or to Epic, MyOchsner or MyChart.
- A statement from Orlando Health.
- Independent confirmation of the Vortex file count. We did not look at leak sites, underground forums or trackers, and we cite the claim only through outlets that report it.
- KLFY's page blocked a direct fetch; its text was read through a search result, not the page itself.
- A security researcher's report naming Ochsner. Palo Alto Networks Unit 42's Vortex research does not mention Ochsner or Orlando Health.
- Becker's Hospital Review covered the notice, per a headline aggregator, but its page blocked our fetch, so we do not cite it.
